dimension_justifications.soundness: The controlled factorial, lifecycle witnesses, and explicitly bounded claims are thoughtfully designed. However, the supplied PDF does not match the declared frozen SHA-256, and the paper itself reports that recursive code closure for the primary GPU aggregate failed (p. 9, Sec. 7). Moreover, the numerical checks are selected captured-input operator tests rather than independent end-to-end validation (pp. 8 and 18, Secs. 5.2-5.3 and Table 12). These are substantive limitations for an executable audit whose central value is evidence integrity.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The paper is clear, well organized, and unusually candid about what is and is not established (pp. 2, 8-9, and 19). Figures and tables are legible and correctly distinguish explanatory schematics from evidence. Some dense audit terminology and the large number of cohorts/appendices make it difficult to identify which artifacts independently establish each headline claim, but this does not prevent evaluation.
dimension_justifications.contribution: A phase-aware ownership-audit integration for hybrid KV/recurrent state is potentially useful, and the paper positions component mechanisms as prior art (pp. 3 and 17, Tables 9-10). The demonstrated contribution is nevertheless a narrow one-stack case study: one model/runtime/hardware family, sequential schedule, selected operator rows, and targeted positive-control faults. The evidence currently supports an interesting audit template more than a broadly validated systems contribution.

paper_summary: ForkAudit proposes an executable ownership-audit contract for hybrid LLM state, separating shared document KV from request-private append state and phase-dependent recurrent GDN ownership. It evaluates four KV-by-GDN setup cells over eight PG-19 books and fan-outs 1, 8, and 32, reports equality of registered digests, selected dense-FP32 attention and NumPy GDN-oracle checks, nine live fault injections, and allocator deltas. The stated scope excludes performance, scheduler, production-capacity, and broad transfer claims.
strongest_verified_contribution: The strongest supported result is the carefully scoped four-cell ownership factorial: under one fixed Qwen3.5/vLLM configuration and sequential schedule, the reported storage-witness predicates and registered semantic digests agree across ownership cells, while shared-document KV lowers the reported final allocator delta at N=32 (pp. 7-8, Secs. 5.1 and 5.4; Table 2).
strengths: The paper distinguishes logical state, page allocation, allocator counters, and unmeasured service/process capacity instead of conflating memory metrics (p. 6, Sec. 4.4; p. 8, Table 2).
The 2x2 ownership design and adjacent-fan-out comparisons make the tested invariances concrete (pp. 6-8, Secs. 4.2-5.1 and Figure 3).
It correctly labels eight books/ranks as distinct workloads rather than stochastic replicates and avoids unsupported confidence intervals (pp. 9 and 13, Sec. 6 and Table 3).
Limitations are unusually explicit: selected captured-input oracles, no compiled-binary identity, one runtime, sequential execution, and positive-control faults are all acknowledged (pp. 8-9 and 19).
questions: Can the authors provide an immutable, externally checkable source/container/manifest closure for the exact primary GPU run, and explain why Table 5 calls frozen identity 'full' despite the failed terminal recursive code closure reported in Sec. 7?
What held-out or independently generated fault set, including nontrivial common-mode and post-output semantic faults, can establish detection coverage beyond nine intended-gate positive controls?

Can the authors add at least one independent end-to-end validation path or substantially broaden numerical operator coverage across layers, requests, token positions, and model/runtime configurations?

issues.location: Artifact-level identity for the supplied manuscript PDF (whole file; PDF pp. 1-20)
issues.observed_evidence: The declared snapshot SHA-256 is 802c99cf2ec462e41b5343dd204c463b3f4d27d0eb3c601e6489d2765e1e7a27, but the PDF supplied at the mandated path hashes to 73f8628ae23119c6c964e5d86670c5c193162a36d22d320d478e249d74126683. Thus this review cannot verify that the inspected PDF is the declared frozen manuscript.
issues.why_it_matters: Artifact identity is central to the paper's audit contract. A mismatch prevents reliable attribution of the visible claims, tables, and limitations to the stated frozen snapshot.
issues.required_fix: Reissue a single immutable submission artifact whose published SHA-256 matches the bytes reviewers receive, and bind that PDF hash to the claimed package/replay manifest.
issues.verification_test: An independent reviewer downloads the submission PDF and manifest, computes SHA-256, and obtains the declared value before evaluating any replay output.
issues.evidence_needed: A matching PDF digest and a content-addressed manifest that binds the PDF, source closure, protocol, and primary-result receipts.

issues.location: PDF p. 9, Sec. 7; PDF p. 14, Table 5; PDF p. 20, Table 13
issues.observed_evidence: Sec. 7 states that the primary GPU aggregate's terminal recursive code closure failed on post-ledger pycache files and that a new derivative manifest, rather than a closed original-run identifier, binds the raw aggregate and replay. In tension with this, Table 5 marks frozen identity as 'full.' Table 13 lists package paths but does not resolve, within the PDF, the executable-source closure of the original aggregate.
issues.why_it_matters: For a contribution framed as an executable ownership audit, replaying a derivative is weaker than establishing the exact code/environment that produced the primary GPU evidence. This leaves room for source/provenance ambiguity even if the derivative checks internal consistency.
issues.required_fix: Publish a reproducible, content-addressed source and environment closure for the primary run, explicitly define allowable generated-file exclusions before execution, and revise the target status if closure remains incomplete.
issues.verification_test: A clean independent environment reconstructs the primary aggregate from the declared source/container/lockfile and raw inputs; its source-tree and output receipt hashes match the registered manifest.
issues.evidence_needed: Immutable source-tree/container digests, dependency lockfiles, deterministic build instructions, and an independently reproduced primary aggregate.

issues.location: PDF pp. 6-8, Secs. 4.3 and 5.2-5.3; PDF p. 18, Table 12; PDF p. 19, Sec. I
issues.observed_evidence: The dense oracle covers eight pre-specified attention rows conditional on captured post-RoPE inputs, while the NumPy recurrence covers four layers and begins after native q/k normalization. The paper explicitly excludes upstream activation construction, normalization, most GDN layers, and end-to-end logits from independent validation. Cross-arm agreement otherwise relies on candidate-produced canonical hashes/digests.
issues.why_it_matters: Agreement among ownership arms is a useful relational check but cannot rule out shared implementation errors. The selected operator-level oracles do not independently validate the end-to-end semantics needed to elevate the audit from internal consistency to robust correctness evidence.
issues.required_fix: Add an independent end-to-end reference or differential implementation where feasible, and expand predeclared operator sampling across layers, token positions, queries, fan-outs, and at least one additional relevant runtime/model configuration.
issues.verification_test: Blindly selected held-out requests and layers are evaluated by the independent path; report raw numerical error distributions, threshold rationale, and any failures rather than only pass counts.
issues.evidence_needed: Archived independent-reference outputs or reproducible sidecars for a broader predeclared sample, plus cross-runtime/model results that separate common-mode errors from ownership-factor effects.

issues.location: PDF pp. 6 and 8, Secs. 4.5 and 5.3; PDF p. 16, Table 7; PDF pp. 18-19, Sec. H and Sec. I
issues.observed_evidence: All nine injected faults are targeted positive controls designed to reach named gates, mostly at N=2. M8 reaches only an injected sentinel, and M9 reaches a later assertion after gate suppression; both abort before semantic outputs. While claims clearly scope sensitivity no detection completeness. Thus not grounds 4 maybe still major relative "executable audit validates", not a fault coverage claim.
issues.why_it_matters: Intended-gate reachability validates that these specific checks are live, but it does not establish sensitivity to realistic, unforeseen, common-mode, or output-level faults. The current evidence should not be read as broad validation of audit coverage.
issues.required_fix: Use a preregistered held-out mutation campaign with independently generated faults, include post-output semantic corruptions and benign perturbations, and report false positives, escapes, wrong-gate outcomes, and coverage by fault class.
issues.verification_test: Evaluate the frozen gate map on a concealed held-out fault suite and publish the full confusion matrix and per-class outcomes.
issues.evidence_needed: A held-out fault corpus and complete outcome matrix, including negative controls and output-level effects.

issues.location: PDF p. 8, Table 2; PDF p. 9, Sec. 6; PDF pp. 13 and 15, Table 3 and Table 6
issues.observed_evidence: Table 2 reports medians over eight ranks and says rank values coincide, while Sec. 6 and Table 3 clarify that ranks are distinct workloads rather than stochastic replicates. The PDF gives no per-rank values, range, or workload-level sensitivity for the primary allocator deltas.
issues.why_it_matters: The deterministic allocator result is valid for the frozen setup, but summary medians across distinct books can be mistaken for replicated statistical evidence and make workload sensitivity difficult to assess.
issues.required_fix: Report the eight raw values or a compact range/min-max table, clearly label the estimand as a fixed-stack deterministic measurement, and add length/alignment or workload sensitivity sweeps if making any broader memory statement.
issues.verification_test: Recompute every summarized delta from the released per-rank measurements and confirm that conclusions remain under the added geometry/workload sweep.
issues.evidence_needed: Per-rank allocator endpoints and predeclared sensitivity measurements over meaningful prefix/page-tail conditions.

ethics_concerns: No material ethics concern is established by the PDF. The ethics statement appropriately notes use of PG-19 and that broader deployment effects are outside scope (p. 12, Sec. A).
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was generated by an LLM agent from the manuscript PDF and supplied rubric/schema; it must be treated as an internal automated review.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A supplied PDF whose SHA-256 matches the declared frozen snapshot, bound to an immutable manuscript/package manifest.
A clean, independently reproduced primary GPU aggregate from an exact source/container/environment closure.
Predeclared, broader independent validation that includes end-to-end or cross-implementation checks and reports all outcomes.
A held-out mutation campaign with realistic fault classes, false-positive/escape outcomes, and output-level consequences.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Confirmation that the PDF hash mismatch corresponds to untracked manuscript/result changes or cannot be reconciled to a frozen package.
Failure of an independent replay to reproduce the reported digest equalities, storage predicates, numerical-oracle bounds, or allocator endpoints.
Evidence that selected oracle rows, fault gates, or memory summaries were chosen after observing candidate outcomes without valid preregistration.
review_limitations: This was a PDF-only blind review; no code, raw artifacts, manifests, or external evidence files were inspected.
The supplied PDF did not match the declared snapshot hash, so conclusions about the declared frozen manuscript are necessarily provisional.
